accepted_baseline_context: main 12fad34 at the historical planning review; authoritative classifications copied from api.json. Frozen checkpoints describe that review, not current execution state; consult work_items.json.
scope_statement: Exactly 477 inventoried public entries across 20 modules, plus a separate 29-class/284-static-member follow-up. Other namespaces, instance fields, runtime-generated attributes and future upstream additions remain outside the current static inventory; this is not an exhaustive entire-library completion claim.
algorithm_count_note: 26 source-backed identity aliases are namespace routes, not additional algorithms. The remaining canonical routes also include wrappers/classes/assets and are not an algorithm-completion count.

common_policy.scope: Planning proposals, not live execution state. See coverage/work_items.json and coverage/EXECUTION_PLAN.md for current assignments and authorization. This document changes no API, evidence or measured-speed status.
common_policy.existing_proofs: Existing strict/bitwise/source-qualified contracts and frozen evidence remain unchanged. A new prospective policy cannot relax them or relabel old failures.
common_policy.structural: Exact signature/default/return container, dtype/shape/layout, integer results, labels, tie and branch decisions, warning/error classes/messages/order, callbacks, mutation/alias/state and namespace identity where the public contract specifies them.
common_policy.floating: Before observing candidate results, declare per-output dtype/conditioning-aware rtol/atol or ULP bounds from algorithm stability and application needs, plus nonfinite/signed-zero rules. Validate with untouched holdouts. A separate bitwise track is mandatory for strict existing scopes or contracts requiring exact arithmetic. Numerical allclose alone cannot excuse changed labels, convergence branches or errors.
common_policy.discovery: Routes below are proposed engineering paths, not validated behavior. Inspect pinned 0.26.0 source and capture contract cases before implementing; ambiguity is an open contract question, not permission to guess.
common_policy.acceptance: Freeze public original cases; scalar typed kernel and actual public wrapper; fallback disabled for claimed native scope; scalar/SIMD and one/multiple-global-worker checks; actual supported build/profile/SDK gates; isolated one-worker public-call comparisons with preserved regressions. Metadata/provider adapters use appropriate contract checks and do not receive image-kernel credit.
common_policy.benchmark: Proposal, not measurement: use identical pinned inputs/options and predeclared parity policy; preserve source/package/runtime/CPU/dispatch/provider identities; xx.set_num_threads(1) and matching upstream BLAS/FFT/OpenMP limits. Warm appropriately, alternate/paired repeated runs, retain raw samples and every slower case. Run alone, without concurrent builds/tests or changing files used by a running benchmark. Report allocation-inclusive public latency; optional core-only diagnostics are labeled separately.
common_policy.providers: An owned C++ objective cannot be satisfied by NumPy/SciPy image-algorithm forwarding. Python metadata, user callbacks, GUI, codec, Dask and estimator objects are explicit ecosystem boundaries. Any retained numerical provider is named; standalone C++ completion needs the relevant reviewed native backend, licenses, ABI/wheel/SDK profiles and its own parity/performance gates.
common_policy.parallelism: Default one process-global worker budget; optional workers only for independent/proven-equivalent work, no nested uncontrolled pools. SIMD is a feasibility proposal; exact ordered or graph/event cores may stay serial. No universal speedup promise.
common_policy.priority: Waves are relative dependency/effort priorities, not strict global barriers or a scope reduction. Family capabilities are menus; each row has separate mandatory route dependencies. Existing native-partial entries may need extensive uncovered-domain work despite a small next increment.

wave_definitions.W0: Review frozen ready/private checkpoints and close their existing qualification/performance gates; no new algorithm credit before acceptance.
wave_definitions.W1: Cheap independent kernels, wrappers and selected existing native-partial contract closure; exact formulas/LUTs and already-owned kernels first.
wave_definitions.W2: Shared neighborhood, histogram/order, connectivity and reconstruction primitives and their consumers.
wave_definitions.W3: Geometry, resampling composition, small solvers and geometric class state/member closure.
wave_definitions.W4: Distance/FFT/multiscale features, registration and restoration; choose reviewed backends before dependent optimization.
wave_definitions.W5: Dependent graph, segmentation and specialized model/solver pipelines with exact event/tie/state semantics.
wave_definitions.P: Independent provider/assets/metadata lane starts alongside W1; explicit adapter boundary is useful progress but not native arithmetic completion.

effort_definitions.XS: Small owned table/alias/metadata audit; excludes full downstream closure.
effort_definitions.S: One bounded direct kernel, adapter or extension of an existing kernel; provider/back-end replacements excluded.
effort_definitions.M: Several shared passes, nontrivial boundary semantics or a moderate solver/backend wrapper.
effort_definitions.L: Stateful, iterative, stochastic, topology-sensitive or broad compatibility surface; split into reviewable contracts.
effort_definitions.XL: Reserved for a separately scoped backend/catalogue replacement; not a calendar estimate.

shared_primitives.array: Typed strided buffers, dtype/range conversion, allocation, overlap and error admission; reuse current bindings and convert.cpp; preserve Python object protocol at the adapter.
shared_primitives.pointwise: Existing scalar/SIMD color, contrast, alpha and distance formulas; prefer direct formulas or bounded LUTs, preserve branch decisions and saturation.
shared_primitives.reduce: Existing typed reductions and integral scans; add stable grouped sums/moments with explicitly ordered or declared-tolerance arithmetic.
shared_primitives.histogram: Existing contrast, threshold and rank histograms; shared dense/sparse counts, CDFs, sorted ranks and stable tie handling.
shared_primitives.neighborhood: Existing Gaussian, sparse/separable convolution, stencil, median and flat morphology kernels; centralize halo, boundary and footprint handling.
shared_primitives.components: Existing connected-component labels, component consumers and array maps; deterministic union-find/label numbering and component statistics.
shared_primitives.order_graph: Stable sorted traversal, priority queues, adjacency and union-find for reconstruction, max trees and graph fronts; serial reference ordering first.
shared_primitives.geometry: Rasterization, point-in-polygon, contour lookup tables and topology; reuse explicit integer recurrences and licensed upstream tables where appropriate.
shared_primitives.resample: Existing spline/resample/resize and projective kernels; reusable coordinate mapping, interpolation, prefilter and clipping.
shared_primitives.small_solver: Small QR/SVD/eigensystem/linear solves with license/profile-reviewed C++ dependency or existing native primitive; do not port all of SciPy.
shared_primitives.sparse_solver: CSR/COO assembly plus license/profile-reviewed sparse direct/iterative C++ solver; freeze convergence, degeneracy and ordering contracts.
shared_primitives.fft: License/profile-reviewed real/complex N-D FFT backend with explicit normalization, padding, cache and one-worker control; backend choice remains open.
shared_primitives.distance: Exact separable Euclidean distance transform and nearest-site indices; spatial search for point sets; explicit tie ordering and anisotropic spacing.
shared_primitives.rng: Pinned Generator/seed/state adapter and draw-order contract; a new C++ generator requires bit-generator/state/distribution parity or a separately declared noncompatible API.
shared_primitives.assets: Pinned asset manifest with resource URL/path, hash, per-asset license, cache/offline/error behavior; image codecs and archive/NPY readers are explicit dependencies.
shared_primitives.provider: Thin Python adapter for optional codecs, estimators, plotting, lazy arrays and object protocols; keep provider availability/errors honest and separate from native arithmetic.
shared_primitives.workers: Existing process-global worker limit, default one; one budget across nested calls; no private pools or provider-thread oversubscription.

point.title: Pointwise formulas and conversions
point.simd: Reuse vector lanes for independent pixels; scalar tails and exceptional branches remain equivalent.
point.workers: Partition disjoint pixel ranges above a measured threshold; default one and shared global budget.
point.numerical_policy: Exact dtype, clipping, integer rounding, branch and warning behavior; predeclare dtype-aware floating tolerances, preserving any existing bitwise contract.
point.benchmark_recipe: Contiguous and strided uint8/float32/float64 images; tiny/512x512/2048x2048; time public allocation and conversion as well as optional kernel-only diagnostic.
point.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

reduce.title: Reductions, histograms and moments
reduce.simd: Vectorize sample transforms or independent accumulators only under the declared reduction policy.
reduce.workers: Thread local counts/partials with fixed merge where allowed; serial for exact ordered reductions.
reduce.numerical_policy: Exact counts, tie outcomes, dtype and ordering; predeclare error bounds for floating reductions and test cancellation/nonfinite inputs.
reduce.benchmark_recipe: Tiny and large arrays, repeated/unique distributions, sparse masks, strided layouts; retain allocation-inclusive timing.
reduce.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

stencil.title: Neighborhood and separable filters
stencil.simd: Reuse SIMD across independent output pixels and existing separable passes; handle borders/tails explicitly.
stencil.workers: Disjoint output tiles with read-only halos; avoid parallel writes to overlapping out buffers.
stencil.numerical_policy: Exact boundaries, footprint origins, dtype/out rules; freeze floating tolerance before comparison and retain strict scopes.
stencil.benchmark_recipe: 2D/3D images with narrow/wide kernels, border-heavy tiny inputs, masks, channel axes and strided/output-buffer cases.
stencil.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

rank.title: Rolling histogram rank operations
rank.simd: Reuse existing rolling histogram SIMD/support scans; vectorize independent windows only when feedback admission permits.
rank.workers: Independent scan strips with private histograms; certified feedback/overlap stays serial; global workers default one.
rank.numerical_policy: Exact histogram counts, quantile/tie comparisons, integer division, signed-char shifts, masked centers and captured-bin stores; preserve frozen strict proofs.
rank.benchmark_recipe: Reuse frozen rank benchmark cases including large windowed histograms, noise-filter regressions, percentile and bilateral thresholds; add uncovered contracts as new IDs.
rank.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

component.title: Labels and component consumers
component.simd: Vectorize predicates/count scans and remapping; union-find ordering remains explicit.
component.workers: Serial reference labeling first; independent component/statistic passes can partition after stable IDs exist.
component.numerical_policy: Exact labels, background, connectivity, output dtype, integer counts, ties and aliasing.
component.benchmark_recipe: Sparse/dense/noisy labels, all-background/all-connected, large label IDs, 2D/3D and strided outputs.
component.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

footprint.title: Footprint construction and decomposition
footprint.simd: Vectorize coordinate predicates for large dense footprints; tiny metadata/sequences gain little.
footprint.workers: Usually serial; only large independent fills may use the global budget.
footprint.numerical_policy: Exact footprint cells, dtype, shape, decomposition sequence/order and iteration counts.
footprint.benchmark_recipe: Radius/shape sweeps, strict/non-strict boundaries, dense and sequence output; include tiny construction overhead.
footprint.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

draw.title: Raster coordinates and geometric masks
draw.simd: Vectorize independent membership/coverage tests; ordered Bresenham/anti-alias recurrences stay scalar.
draw.workers: Serial ordered coordinate emission; parallel independent rows only with stable output concatenation.
draw.numerical_policy: Exact coordinate order, endpoint/clip rules and duplicate pixels; declared tolerance for anti-alias values.
draw.benchmark_recipe: Short/long/degenerate primitives, clipped and unclipped output, small and megapixel masks; include coordinate allocation.
draw.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

geometry.title: Contours, topology and shape geometry
geometry.simd: Vectorize independent cell classification, geometry tests or triangle measures; traversal/topology resolution stays ordered.
geometry.workers: Parallel independent cells/components with stable stitching; serial global topology decisions.
geometry.numerical_policy: Exact topology, connectivity, tie/ordering contracts; predeclare coordinate/solver tolerances separately.
geometry.benchmark_recipe: Small degenerate and large structured/noisy 2D/3D geometry, open/closed boundaries and anisotropic spacing.
geometry.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

resample.title: Coordinate mapping and image resampling
resample.simd: Reuse projective/spline SIMD for independent points/output pixels; scalar exceptional coordinates.
resample.workers: Disjoint output tiles; sequential dependency between pyramid levels, one global worker budget.
resample.numerical_policy: Exact shape/coordinate conventions, clipping, dtype, errors and branch choices; interpolation tolerance predeclared and strict historical profiles retained.
resample.benchmark_recipe: Tiny/HD images and volumes, integer/float, contiguous/reversed inputs, affine/nonlinear maps, all supported interpolation/boundary modes.
resample.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

model.title: Geometric model fitting and state
model.simd: Vectorize batched transforms and residuals; tiny QR/SVD/iteration control need not use SIMD.
model.workers: Fit/control flow serial; parallel independent residual blocks or independent user-requested fits under global limit.
model.numerical_policy: Exact state transitions, failure objects, parameter conventions, rank/degeneracy decisions; prospective conditioning-aware solve/residual tolerance.
model.benchmark_recipe: Separate construction/fit/predict/residual calls for minimal, degenerate, ill-conditioned and large point sets; include object/public-call overhead.
model.native_provider_frontier: C++ small-solver/coordinate kernels plus own Python class state and descriptors; retaining NumPy/SciPy fit arithmetic is a provider frontier, not standalone C++ completion.

tree.title: Reconstruction and component trees
tree.simd: Vectorize admission, min/max and remapping scans; priority/parent propagation is data dependent.
tree.workers: Serial exact queue/tree core first; independent preparation/output or separately proven component partitions only.
tree.numerical_policy: Exact plateau/tie order, connectivity, parent/traverser consistency, integer dtype, offsets and seed-mask constraints.
tree.benchmark_recipe: Plateaus, ramps, noisy/nested components, sparse markers, 2D/3D and dtype extremes; include tree construction versus reuse separately.
tree.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

distance.title: Distance transforms and spatial queries
distance.simd: Vectorize distance evaluation and independent line envelopes; nearest-site tie decisions explicit.
distance.workers: Parallel independent transform lines or point-query batches; serial dimension passes and stable reductions.
distance.numerical_policy: Exact selected-site/tie and empty-set contracts; spacing-aware floating tolerance predeclared.
distance.benchmark_recipe: Sparse/dense binary masks and point clouds, anisotropic 2D/3D grids, equidistant sites and large distances.
distance.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

fft.title: Fourier filters and spectral restoration
fft.simd: Use reviewed FFT backend vectorization plus SIMD spectral multiplication; preserve normalization and real/complex conventions.
fft.workers: FFT threads obey global budget; no nested pools; independent channels only when backend is single-threaded.
fft.numerical_policy: Exact shapes, padding, phase/normalization and clipping; predeclare complex/real numerical tolerance and separate strict track when required.
fft.benchmark_recipe: Odd/even and prime/composite 2D/3D shapes, real/complex inputs, cold versus warmed FFT plans, allocation-inclusive public calls.
fft.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

feature.title: Feature pipelines and descriptors
feature.simd: Vectorize gradients, response pixels and descriptor distance blocks; candidate ordering and suppression remain explicit.
feature.workers: Independent scales/keypoints/blocks can partition under one global budget with stable output ordering.
feature.numerical_policy: Exact candidate/descriptor shape, mask, ordering, tie and RNG decisions; declared tolerance for response and normalized descriptor floats.
feature.benchmark_recipe: Blank/textured images, edge-heavy images, tiny and megapixel sizes, sparse/dense keypoints; report detect/extract/full pipeline separately.
feature.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

iterative.title: Iterative dense image solvers
iterative.simd: Vectorize independent stencil/update pixels subject to Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel update order; serial convergence decisions.
iterative.workers: Tile independent updates with barriers between iterations; serial or coloring only if proven equivalent for dependent updates.
iterative.numerical_policy: Freeze update order, stopping condition, dtype, callback and warning behavior; predeclare residual/output tolerance and test iteration count separately.
iterative.benchmark_recipe: Tiny/HD/3D images, flat/edge/noisy inputs, short/default/long iteration counts; record actual iteration/convergence behavior and total public latency.
iterative.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

graph.title: Graph fronts, cuts and sparse operators
graph.simd: Vectorize edge weights/CSR preparation and batch residuals; heaps, hooks and mutable traversal are serial first.
graph.workers: Independent edge construction/components/batch shortest paths only; mutable queues and callback event order remain serial.
graph.numerical_policy: Exact graph/node/edge identities, mutation/callback order and tie outcomes; predeclare sparse-solver tolerance and convergence/warning policy.
graph.benchmark_recipe: Small disconnected/degenerate and large grid/region graphs, varied degree/weights; separate graph build, solver and public wrapper costs.
graph.native_provider_frontier: C++ graph/solver core; NetworkX/SciPy sparse/plotting object adapters remain explicit providers until independently replaced.

segment.title: Segmentation and ordered region algorithms
segment.simd: Vectorize per-pixel features/distances; merges, heaps and topology-changing decisions retain exact order.
segment.workers: Parallel independent preprocessing/local assignments; ordered merges/front propagation serial until proven equivalent.
segment.numerical_policy: Exact labels, tie/order/connectivity, seed/RNG consumption and callbacks; declared tolerance for continuous energies without changing label branches silently.
segment.benchmark_recipe: Flat/noisy/region-rich 2D/3D images, sparse/dense markers, anisotropic spacing and masks; include all preprocessing and post-labeling.
segment.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

random.title: Random generators and stochastic helpers
random.simd: Vectorize deterministic transforms after fixed-order random draws; do not swap RNG algorithm for speed.
random.workers: RNG state consumption serial unless a source-equivalent partition is proven; downstream independent image arithmetic may parallelize.
random.numerical_policy: Exact seed/Generator state, draw count/order and distribution algorithm where interchangeability requires it; distribution-only tests cannot prove seeded parity.
random.benchmark_recipe: Fixed saved RNG states, tiny/large output shapes and all distribution/mode branches; reset equivalent state outside each timed call.
random.native_provider_frontier: Native C++ arithmetic target; Python retains documented array/protocol adaptation. Provider use is separately disclosed.

asset.title: Bundled/downloaded data assets
asset.simd: No image-algorithm SIMD claim; codec implementations may have separately reported acceleration.
asset.workers: No native worker claim; controlled fetch/decode concurrency only with cache locking and provider contracts.
asset.numerical_policy: Exact bytes/hashes and decoded shape/dtype/value/orientation/container contract; licenses/cache/offline/errors independently verified.
asset.benchmark_recipe: Noncompute boundary: separate warm-cache decode/local file latency from cold authorized fetch; never compare network timing as C++ kernel speed.
asset.native_provider_frontier: Asset manifest/cache and codec adapter first. This preserves API behavior but is not a native image algorithm or standalone C++ codec completion.

io.title: I/O and collection adapters
io.simd: No wrapper SIMD claim; native copy/parse kernels or codec SIMD measured separately.
io.workers: Keep stack/cache/event semantics serial; provider codec threads explicitly bounded when available.
io.numerical_policy: Exact filenames/order, frame/dtype/metadata, warnings, errors, lazy loading, mutation and file side effects.
io.benchmark_recipe: Noncompute boundary: local fixture round trips/parse/collection access; warm/cold-cache timing reported separately, no network in compute benchmarks.
io.native_provider_frontier: Preserve optional imageio/Pillow/tifffile-style providers behind adapters first; standalone C++ support requires explicit licensed codec/container selection and parity.

ui.title: Plotting and GUI adapters
ui.simd: No SIMD for GUI/event loop; image preprocessing can reuse native kernels.
ui.workers: GUI state/event callbacks remain on the provider event thread; no parallel UI claim.
ui.numerical_policy: Exact return artists/state, coordinate transforms, callback order, cancellation and provider missing/error behavior.
ui.benchmark_recipe: Noncompute boundary: scripted headless artist/state/interaction fixtures; optional render latency separately, no native-kernel speed ratio.
ui.native_provider_frontier: Matplotlib/GUI adapter is the intended compatibility boundary; native preprocessing is counted separately, not as replacement of the GUI provider.

learn.title: Optional estimators and learned models
learn.simd: Native feature normalization/batched distance or responsibility arithmetic can vectorize; arbitrary estimator methods are provider calls.
learn.workers: Adapter respects estimator threading; future native batch prediction/EM uses global budget with deterministic reductions.
learn.numerical_policy: Exact estimator identity/state, feature order, fit/predict calls, labels/errors and RNG behavior; tolerance separately specified for optional native solver.
learn.benchmark_recipe: Noncompute adapter boundary initially: instrument estimator calls and payloads; benchmark feature extraction separately. A future C++ solver needs fit/predict timing on identical models.
learn.native_provider_frontier: Keep scikit-learn/user-estimator adapter for public interchangeability. A standalone C++ GMM/EM or classifier backend is a separate explicitly scoped solver, not implied by the adapter.

metadata.title: Metadata, state and views
metadata.simd: No SIMD for type/state/view construction; vectorize only an explicit copy/fill when material.
metadata.workers: Serial metadata/state operations; no process-global worker benefit claimed.
metadata.numerical_policy: Exact identity/sharing, strides, readonly flags, dtype, signatures, inheritance, warnings/errors and state transitions.
metadata.benchmark_recipe: Noncompute boundary: descriptor/signature/state/alias fixtures; optional microbenchmarks only when overhead matters, not image-kernel speed claims.
metadata.native_provider_frontier: Own metadata or thin object-protocol wrapper is legitimate API behavior; Python/NumPy view/state machinery is not claimed as standalone C++ arithmetic.
